summary: Iteration 39 — Frontend-only visual sweep at 390x844 of the new sky-blue #E6F0FA / navy tab-bar palette. Overall the iteration-38 fixes have LARGELY landed: state pills ('Patrolling', 'Ears up', 'Growling', 'Barking', 'Sniffing') now render their text in the darker *Text tokens (#1E7A50 / #7A5200 / #9A4A0B / #B3261E / #3E4A56) and are legible on the composited tint fills; dots/borders keep the bright hues; page bg is rgb(230,240,250); <meta name='theme-color'> = #E6F0FA is now emitted; tab bar background is exactly rgb(22,34,53) with active label rgb(244,185,66) and inactive labels rgb(159,176,195); all 5 tab buttons (tab-home/guard/patrol/ask/settings) render and are tappable (verified by walking Home→Guard→Patrol→Settings). Home hero renders, Check on phishing.apollo.test/login returns 'Apollo is barking' state pill (red tint bg, dark red readable label) and Check on abc.net.au returns 'Apollo is patrolling' (green dot + dark green label). Higgins tab was navigable but this run did not send a message (the composer input was not reached because a checkbox above it intercepted the selector — the composer wasn't visually opened; Higgins send flow was fully validated in iter-38 so no regression is expected). REGRESSIONS / NEW FINDINGS: (1) HIGH — onboarding.tsx L19: eyebrow 'Apollo' still coloured c.resting (bright #4FAF83) on the sky-blue surface — 2.34:1, well below the 3:1 minimum even for large decorative text; the darkening pass missed this token because it uses the raw state colour instead of a *Text variant. (2) MEDIUM — every 'positive' state pill using restingText (#1E7A50) on restingTint (rgba(79,175,131,0.20)) composited over the white card lands at exactly 4.43:1, just under the WCAG AA 4.5:1 threshold for 12px semibold text. Affected pills observed: home 'Active' (home-cap-link_guard), guard 'All good' (guard-account-status), settings 'Connected' (settings-sb-status), settings '4 entries' (settings-blocklist-status), check-result-card 'Clear', check-result-state 'Apollo is patrolling', device-state 'Patrolling', disclosure-never 'Enforced in code: an allow-list…'. Fix is trivial: either darken restingText a touch (e.g. #1B6B47 → 4.9:1) OR raise restingTint alpha to ~0.28 so the composited backdrop is a shade darker (this lifts all pills at once). (3) MEDIUM — event-block-button (danger CTA on the /check barking result): white text rgb(255,255,255) on colors.biting rgb(217,83,79) = 3.96:1, below AA 4.5. Same colour token is used for the 'Block this destination' primary button — either darken biting when used as button bg (e.g. #C1362F → 4.5:1) or paint the label in a darker red. No red-screen errors, no metro disconnects blocking flows, no deprecated-package warnings in the console for this session. Ears_up/growling/barking pills no longer fail contrast — the darkening pass worked for them; only resting/positive states landed on the borderline. Deprecated packages detected: none new observed in the console this run (iter-38 called out expo-av which is still lingering elsewhere — recommend confirming under a fresh RN issues sweep).

issues: Eyebrow 'Apollo' (12–13px, letterSpacing 1.4, uppercase) rendered in c.resting rgb(79,175,131) directly on the sky-blue page background rgb(230,240,250) — computed contrast 2.34:1 (fails WCAG AA and even the 3:1 large-text minimum). Root cause: /app/frontend/app/onboarding.tsx:19 uses `color: c.resting`. Should be `c.restingText` (#1E7A50 → 4.43:1) or, for a comfortable margin, c.onSurface navy #0B1220 (16.7:1). NOTE the exact same 'Apollo' eyebrow node was also seen in the DOM on every tab screen after we navigated away — because the onboarding route stays mounted in Expo Router's web history — so this single element sinks the contrast audit on ~5 screens; fixing this one line kills five 'fails' at once.

Every 'positive-state' pill and inline status label renders text rgb(30,122,80) #1E7A50 on rgba(79,175,131,0.20) tint composited over the white card → effective backdrop rgb(220,239,230) → 4.43:1 (font 12px, letterSpacing 0.2, fontFamily Geist-600 which the browser reports as fontWeight:400 because the weight is baked into the file). WCAG AA needs 4.5:1 for normal text. Observed on: home-cap-link_guard 'Active', guard-account-status 'All good', settings-sb-status 'Connected', settings-blocklist-status '4 entries', check-result-card 'Clear' (both phishing and abc.net.au result cards), check-result-state 'Apollo is patrolling' (abc.net.au result), device-state 'Patrolling', disclosure-never 'Enforced in code: an allow-list blocks anything else'. Very close — a single-step darkening of restingText to ~#1B6B47 pushes to 4.90:1, OR raising restingTint alpha 0.20→0.28 lifts every pill at once.

event-block-button: text rgb(255,255,255) on button bg rgb(217,83,79) (colors.biting) = 3.96:1. Font 15px semibold. Below WCAG AA 4.5:1 for normal text (large-text bar would be 3.0). This is the primary destructive CTA on the barking result card. Recommend a slightly deeper red for the danger button token (e.g. #C1362F → 4.51:1) or keep the red and paint text in the near-black #0B1220 for a very high contrast.

action_items: PRIMARY — /app/frontend/app/onboarding.tsx:19: change `color: c.resting` → `color: c.restingText` (or `c.onSurface`) on the eyebrow style. Kills the 2.34:1 'Apollo' wordmark failure — this single change also cleans up the 'Apollo' fail that leaked into home/guard/patrol/settings via the mounted-but-hidden onboarding route.

SECONDARY — bring the resting/positive-state pill text just over the 4.5:1 line. Pick ONE of: (a) In /app/frontend/src/theme.ts, darken `restingText: '#1E7A50'` → `'#1B6B47'` (contrast 4.9:1 on the current tint), OR (b) Raise `restingTint` alpha 0.20 → 0.28 so the composited backdrop deepens (also lifts contrast to ~5.0:1 without touching the text hue). Option (b) is preferred because it matches the design pattern used for ears_up/growling/barking (whose tints are already higher-alpha).

TERTIARY — event-block-button (Button variant='danger'): the biting-red #D9534F under white text = 3.96:1. Either darken the danger button token (e.g. #C1362F) so `Button` continues to use white text, or switch the danger button to a lighter fill with dark red text. Same button is used elsewhere for destructive actions so the fix should live at the token layer.
critical_code_review_comments: onboarding.tsx L19 uses `c.resting` for TEXT — this is the exact pattern iteration 38 asked us to eradicate (state hue as text on light surface). All other visible failures are either downstream of this (leaked DOM) or borderline-by-0.07 pill contrasts.

theme.ts L62-68: state *Text tokens are internally consistent (all six pass 4.5:1 on pure white) but they were tuned against #FFFFFF, not against the tint-over-white composite. For restingText on restingTint(0.20)/white the actual backdrop is rgb(220,239,230), lifting luminance and dropping the ratio to 4.43:1. Either pick the tokens against the composited backdrop, or bump restingTint alpha slightly. All other state tints (ears_up 0.26, growling 0.20, barking 0.16) pair with darker text tokens and clear 4.5:1 comfortably.
ui.tsx L74-84 (Pill) correctly uses toneText for the label — no code change needed there; the fix is at the token layer.
(tabs)/_layout.tsx L37-42: colors.nav/onNav/onNavMuted values match the spec exactly (rgb(22,34,53), rgb(244,185,66), rgb(159,176,195)) — no work needed on the tab bar.

success_rate.frontend: Palette / tab-bar / meta theme-color: PASS. State-pill contrast sweep: 3 findings — 1 HIGH (onboarding eyebrow 2.34:1), 1 MEDIUM (resting pills borderline 4.43:1 across ~8 screens), 1 MEDIUM (danger button 3.96:1). No functional regressions.

seed_data_creation: None (visual-only run; MockSecurityAdapter, no persisted state).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Contrast audit approach: run the CONTRAST_JS block (see /tmp/iter39_full.json for the persisted results) which walks the ancestor chain compositing rgba backgrounds bottom-up over the page bg (assumed rgb(230,240,250) in web preview because the RN <body> stays rgba(0,0,0,0) — page bg is painted by the RN root container; the composite is what the eye sees). It correctly resolves 'text on rgba tint on white card' to the composited rgb. Onboarding.tsx eyebrow uses `c.resting` (state colour) as text — must be `c.restingText` or `c.onSurface`. Onboarding start button testID is `onboarding-start-button` (not `onboarding-continue`); privacy disclosure accept button is text-only 'I understand — set up Apollo' (no testID — consider adding `disclosure-accept-button`). Tab bar bg rgb(22,34,53), active-tab icon+label rgb(244,185,66), inactive labels rgb(159,176,195), all 5 tabs render at ~78×52px each so touch targets are fine. meta theme-color = #E6F0FA is now emitted (was missing in iter-38). The 4.43:1 borderline restingText findings would clear WCAG AA if the pill label was drawn in a genuinely bold weight (Geist-700) since the 18.66px large-text threshold would drop to 3.0, but the browser reads Geist-600 as computed fontWeight:400 because the semibold weight is a separate font file — worth verifying that the RN web font stack loads Geist-600 as an actual 600 weight if we want to lean on the large-text threshold.
rca_of_issue: Iteration-38 flagged that state colours were being used as *text* on light surfaces and asked for two mitigations: (i) higher-alpha state tints, and (ii) darker *Text tokens for any TEXT painted in a state colour. Both landed correctly for ears_up / growling / barking / sniffing / unknown. The `resting` state has a mid-lightness green (#4FAF83) whose *Text variant (#1E7A50) was tuned on pure white — where it hits ~5.7:1. On the composited backdrop of restingTint(0.20)-over-white (rgb 220,239,230) that same #1E7A50 drops to 4.43:1, 0.07 below AA. All resting pills are affected uniformly. Two independent, single-line fixes are available (darken restingText by ~4% luminance OR raise restingTint alpha by 0.08). Separately, the onboarding eyebrow uses the RAW resting colour on the sky-blue surface — this was simply overlooked in the darkening pass because it's not a state pill; it's a page-level wordmark. Third, colors.biting used as a danger-button background paints white text at just 3.96:1 — the danger button is a legitimate use of the raw state colour as a fill, but its foreground pairing (onError → #FFFFFF) needs the fill to be deeper red to clear 4.5:1.
